## Problem

In the fork-child branch of bool ProcessProgress::start_child_process, failed pthread_sigmask or dup2 returns EXIT_FAILURE. On the audited platform EXIT_FAILURE is 1, converted to true. The failed child can return into controller code after closing its controller descriptors instead of terminating.

## Evidence level

Independently checked source-proven conditional branch. No actual pthread_sigmask/dup2 failure was injected during the audit; the consequences depend on the failing call and remaining slots.

## Reproduction / verification status

Source inspection: follow the return statements at Linux controller lines 576–578 and 605–609 back to the initial/recovery Boolean callers. Proposed regression: inject each child-only setup failure, assert child exit, no controller fallthrough and no child-created extra workers. That injection has not yet been run.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Every post-fork fatal child setup error takes a terminal child-exit path, never a Boolean return into parent/controller execution.
- Inject each covered failure and assert process tree, cleanup/reaping, parent status and absence of unintended worker spawning.
- Audit neighboring child-return branches and use child-safe termination semantics. Keep rare fault branches distinct from ordinary launch behavior.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.
